endorsements.quote: AI-derived tools should thus serve as a decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinical judgment.

Clinicians must be equipped to critically evaluate AI research, understand methodological and ethical limitations such as algorithmic bias, data privacy, and patient autonomy, and to effectively translate findings into clinical practice (Charow et al., 2021 ).

unlisted_practices: Professional organizations should establish clear AI competency standards, educational programs, and implementation support that preserves holistic patient care.
Healthcare providers should clearly communicate AI capabilities and limitations to patients and families to obtain informed consent.

Neuropsychology departments should adapt existing AI governance protocols, including documentation templates, patient consent language, audit schedules, staff training requirements, and incident response procedures, as models.
Educational programs should demonstrate how AI enhances rather than replaces clinical expertise.

screen.reason: This is a perspective paper proposing guidelines and addressing ethical and implementation challenges for integrating AI into neuropsychology.
